chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from some of our companions, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said:

The Imam has ten signs: he is born purified and circumcised; when he falls upon the ground, he falls upon the palms of his hands, raising his voice with the two testimonies; he does not become junub; his eyes sleep but his heart does not sleep; he neither yawns nor stretches; he sees from behind him just as he sees from before him; his excretion has the fragrance of musk, and the earth is entrusted with concealing and swallowing it; when he wears the armor of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), it fits him exactly, and if someone else among the people, tall or short, wears it, it exceeds him by a handspan; and he is one who is spoken to until his days come to an end.

key_terms.الشَّهَادَتَيْنِ: The two testimonies of faith, which he utters at birth.
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: The divinely appointed Imam, described here through distinctive identifying signs.
key_terms.دِرْعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: The armor of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), a sign of rightful succession when it fits the Imam exactly.
key_terms.عَلَامَاتٍ: Signs or markers by which the Imam is recognized.
key_terms.مُحَدَّثٌ: One who is addressed or spoken to, understood as receiving communication from the angels.
key_terms.مُطَهَّرًا: Purified; born in a state of purity.

ai.seo_question: What are the signs and distinguishing characteristics of the Imam in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith describes distinctive signs of the Imam, presenting extraordinary qualities associated with his birth, bodily state, perception, and divine support. It emphasizes the unique status of the Imam and his continuity in receiving divine communication throughout his lifetime.
